claims.text: The applicable alloy is equimolar or nearly equimolar CoCrFeNiTi.
The CoCrFeNiTi alloy is initially in a simple solid-solution state.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy has favorable plasticity.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low hardness.
The starting CoCrFeNiTi alloy has relatively low strength.
Enhanced dynamic recovery is the primary cause of the alloy's relatively low hardness and strength.
Dynamic recovery prevents substantial dislocation accumulation during deformation.
Reduced dislocation accumulation limits work hardening.
Higher testing temperatures promote dynamic recovery in this alloy.
Lower strain rates promote dynamic recovery in this alloy.
Dynamic recovery annihilates or rearranges dislocations.
Low testing temperatures suppress dynamic recovery.
High strain rates suppress dynamic recovery.
Suppressing recovery produces a higher dislocation density.
A higher dislocation density increases hardness.
A higher dislocation density increases yield strength.
Samples deformed under high-strain-rate, low-temperature conditions will have higher dislocation densities than samples deformed under recovery-promoting conditions.
Low-temperature conditions are predicted to produce greater yield strength than elevated-temperature conditions.
The hypothesis applies from room temperature to approximately 200°C and from about 10^-4 s^-1 to 10^2 s^-1.
Grain-boundary effects or nanotwinning may also contribute to the observed mechanical properties.

contradictions.description: The mechanism and prediction state that low-recovery conditions should give higher dislocation density, hardness, and yield strength. The falsification rule instead refers to a reduction in dislocation density and lower hardness and yield strength under low-recovery conditions, reversing the predicted direction.

The design contrasts recovery-promoting conditions with recovery-suppressing conditions, but the falsification rule compares 'low recovery conditions' with conditions that 'suppress recovery,' which describe the same experimental category rather than distinct comparison groups.
